d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 4. The Temperate Region
d.notions: Mixed farming, dairy farming, extensive grain farming, ranching, Mediterranean farming, mechanisation.
d.competence: Learners are able to explain where the imported flour, milk and meat sold in Garoua come from, and how they are produced.
objectives: Describe the main types of farming in the temperate region.
Give examples of countries for each type of farming.
Explain why temperate farming is very productive.
recall: The temperate region has deciduous forests, coniferous forests, Mediterranean vegetation and grasslands.
Its brown forest soils and chernozems are very fertile.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: food products imported from temperate countries.
situation: In a shop in Garoua, Blaise sees bags of wheat flour from France, tins of powdered milk from the Netherlands and bottles of olive oil from Spain.
He wonders how these countries can produce so much food that they sell it to other countries.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Blaise does not understand how temperate countries produce so much food that they sell it abroad.
Which products did Blaise see, and where do they come from?
He saw wheat flour from France, powdered milk from the Netherlands and olive oil from Spain.
What can Cameroon learn from these countries to produce more food?
Cameroon can use machines, improved seeds, fertilisers and good training for farmers.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how farming is done in temperate countries and why it produces so much food.

qa.q: In England and France, many farmers grow crops and rear animals on the same farm. What is this type of farming called?
qa.a: It is called mixed farming. Farmers grow wheat, barley and vegetables, and rear cattle, pigs and sheep.

qa.q: The Netherlands, Denmark and New Zealand rear many cows for milk, butter and cheese. What type of farming is this?
qa.a: It is called dairy farming. The mild, wet climate gives green grass all year.

qa.q: On the Prairies of Canada and the USA, huge farms grow only wheat with large machines. What type of farming is this?
qa.a: It is called extensive commercial grain farming. The Prairies, the Steppes and the Pampas produce huge amounts of wheat.

qa.q: On the Pampas of Argentina and in Australia, animals are reared on huge farms. What are these farms called?
qa.a: They are called ranches. Argentina rears beef cattle, and Australia and New Zealand rear many sheep for wool and meat.

qa.q: Which crops are typical of Mediterranean farming?
qa.a: Mediterranean farmers grow olives, grapes (for wine), citrus fruits and wheat, and they irrigate in the dry summer.

sum.title: I. Types of Farming
sum.intro: The main types of farming in the temperate region are the following:
items: A. Mixed Farming
Mixed farming is the growing of crops and rearing of animals on the same farm, as in England and France.
B. Dairy Farming
Dairy farming is the rearing of cows for milk, butter and cheese, as in the Netherlands, Denmark and New Zealand.
C. Extensive Grain Farming
Extensive grain farming is the growing of wheat on huge farms with machines, as on the Prairies, the Steppes and the Pampas.
D. Ranching
Ranching is the rearing of cattle or sheep on huge farms called ranches, as in Argentina, Australia and New Zealand.
E. Mediterranean Farming
Mediterranean farming is the growing of olives, grapes, citrus fruits and wheat, with irrigation in summer.

qa.q: Why does one farmer in Canada produce much more wheat than one farmer in North Cameroon?
qa.a: He uses tractors and combine harvesters, improved seeds, fertilisers and pesticides, and he farms a much larger area.

qa.q: How do temperate farmers sell their products at good prices?
qa.a: They join cooperatives, which store, process and sell their products. Governments also help them with subsidies.

sum.title: II. Characteristics of Temperate Farming
sum.intro: Temperate farming has the following characteristics:
items: A. Mechanisation
Farmers use tractors, combine harvesters and milking machines, so few workers produce a lot.
B. Science and Inputs
Farmers use improved seeds, fertilisers and pesticides, so yields are high.
C. Commercial Farming
Most products are sold, often abroad. Farmers are organised in cooperatives and helped by the government.

evaluation: Mixed farming is the growing of crops and rearing of animals on the same farm.
Name one country known for dairy farming and one known for ranching.
The Netherlands is known for dairy farming, and Argentina is known for ranching.
Give two reasons why temperate farming is very productive.
Farmers use machines, improved seeds and fertilisers.
remediation: Growing crops and rearing animals on the same farm is called ______ farming.
Rearing cows for milk and cheese is called ______ farming.
Huge farms for rearing cattle are called ______.
The grassland of Canada and the USA that produces wheat is the ______.
A typical Mediterranean crop is the ______.
A machine that cuts and threshes wheat is a combine ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. mixed 2. dairy 3. ranches 4. Prairies 5. olive (or grape) 6. harvester
d.homework: Ask an adult who has lived or travelled in Europe what difficulties people face in winter. Write down two of them.
